record.paper_title: Open problems about regular languages, 35 years later
record.original_question: Let X be a finite maximal code over an alphabet A. Do there always exist polynomials P and S with coefficients in N⟨A⟩ such that 1 − X = P(1 − A)S?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2 For any finite maximal code X over A, there exist two polynomials P, S ∈ N⟨A⟩ such that 1 − X = P(1 − A)S.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $\mathbb{N}\langle A\rangle$ denote the semiring of noncommutative polynomials in the letters of $A$ with coefficients in the nonnegative integers $\mathbb{N}$. A subset $X\subseteq A^+$ is called a code if every word in $A^*$ has at most one factorization as a concatenation of elements of $X$; it is a maximal code if it is not strictly contained in any other code over $A$. We identify any finite subset $Y\subseteq A^*$ with the polynomial $\sum_{w\in Y} w \in \mathbb{N}\langle A\rangle$, so in particular $A$ denotes the polynomial $\sum_{a\in A} a$.

Question: For every finite maximal code $X$ over $A$, do there exist polynomials $P, S \in \mathbb{N}\langle A\rangle$ such that the identity
$$1 - X \;=\; P\,(1 - A)\,S$$
holds in $\mathbb{Z}\langle A\rangle$?
artifact.category_tag: Factorization conjecture for finite maximal codes
artifact.status_search_result: The factorization conjecture (due to Schützenberger) for finite maximal codes is a long-standing open problem. Only partial results are known, e.g. for codes over a binary alphabet with bounded occurrences of one letter, and a recent note (arXiv:1205.2310) addressing special cases, but the general conjecture remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A note on the factorization conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses partial advances on the Schützenberger factorization conjecture for finite maximal codes.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still open in general; only partial results exist.

status_evidence.title: A partial result about the factorization conjecture for finite variable-length codes
status_evidence.snippet: Partial result on the factorization conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Constructing Finite Maximal Codes from Schützenberger Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Family of finite maximal codes verifying the factorization conjecture, with bounded occurrences of b.
status_evidence.claim: Verified for specific subfamilies, but not in general.
